items.description: R1 — "`backup.yml` delivers the staged secret_id on `stat.exists` alone, never checking it against the live role. The staging dir is a persistent per-checkout `tmp/`, so one stale file installs a dead credential permanently." Resolved: before a staged backup secret_id is installed on the OpenBao nodes, the run checks it against the live `backup` AppRole, and a dead one fails the run with a message naming `openbao_rotate_secret_ids=true` (today the delivery at ansible/roles/openbao/tasks/backup.yml:92-100 is gated on `_openbao_staged_secret_id.stat.exists` alone).

There is no silent skip and no automatic re-mint. Each node's own pass installs a staged secret_id only after an AppRole login with the staged role_id and secret_id succeeds; no admin token is needed. A rejected login fails the run, naming `openbao_rotate_secret_ids=true`. The check mints no secret_id, revokes or deletes no credential, and leaves no lasting login token behind. Minting stays behind the operator's `openbao_rotate_secret_ids=true` (default false, ansible/roles/openbao/defaults/main.yml:87).

The remedy the failure names works. A `site-openbao.yml -e openbao_rotate_secret_ids=true` run from the checkout holding the dead staged secret_id completes on the serialized apply (ansible/playbooks/site-openbao.yml:171): the bootstrap host's pass re-stages a fresh secret_id, and every node's pass, the later ones included, proves it by login. The run leaves every OpenBao node holding a secret_id the live `backup` AppRole accepts. Proving this live takes a rotation run, which mints a fresh never-expiring secret_id for all six AppRoles and revokes none of the old ones (ansible/roles/openbao/tasks/approle.yml:329-347). The test phase names that cost and leaves the run to the operator; it does not present the run as a routine proof.

Check mode stays meaningful: a `--check` run from a checkout holding a dead staged secret_id reports the failure, and a `--check` run with no staged secret_id (the drift job's fresh clone) behaves as before.

A run against a fresh cluster before its snapshot restore, where there is no `backup` AppRole to log in against, neither installs the staged secret_id nor fails; it says the backup credential was not delivered. A dead secret_id against a live `backup` role is never reported that way; it still fails the run. (Before the restore nothing has enabled AppRole auth: ansible/roles/openbao/tasks/approle.yml:35-36, :55-65.)

`docs/runbooks/openbao.md` §3 (whole-cluster loss) carries a converge after the snapshot restore, which proves and delivers the backup credential. Today §3 goes converge (step 3), restore (4), verify (5), with no converge after the restore (docs/runbooks/openbao.md:151-191).

R2 — "Every leg of the wrapper is a bare `curl -fsS`, so a failure never says which call broke. Cost three months of misdiagnosis." Resolved: every call the backup wrapper makes — leader check, AppRole login, snapshot, policy list and reads, KV walk and reads, auth and mount reads, upload (ansible/roles/openbao/templates/openbao-backup.sh.j2:29, :38-44, :46, :52-53, :57-58, :73-82, :102-103, :117-122) — names itself on failure, with the HTTP status and, for OpenBao calls, OpenBao's error text.
The wrapper never prints a token, a secret_id or a response body, on failure or success.

R3 — "Followers exit 0 — a dead backup looks healthy fleet-wide. No freshness check anywhere." Per the 2026-09-14 ruling, this slice's criterion is that slice 023 carries it (AnsibleSpecs/slices/backlog/023_backup_freshness_alerting/slice.md, requirement 1), and no phase of this slice delivers any part of backup freshness — backup-server, Prometheus, alert rules, or the validity sent with the upload.

R4 — "the kubelite restart no longer shows up in a --check --diff run of site-k8s.yml". Resolved: in a check-mode run the kubelite restart announces itself as a change on each node it would restart, and check mode still never restarts anything (today ansible/roles/microk8s/handlers/main.yml:40-77 is a `shell` handler with no check-mode handling, hidden by ansible/ansible.cfg:12).

The same check-mode announcement covers `Restart microk8s` and `Rollout-restart coredns` (ansible/roles/microk8s/handlers/main.yml:18-38). By ruling, `Restart microceph OSD daemon` and `Restart microceph MDS daemon` are not covered: their only notifiers are `command` tasks skipped under `--check` (ansible/roles/microceph/tasks/config.yml:90-95, :107-112).
Outside check mode the three handlers behave and report as before, and a converged host still reports `changed=0` under `--check`.

R5 — "the kubelite wait gates on /livez, which is liveness, not the 'serving again' the handler comment claims". Resolved: the kubelite restart waits for readiness — the API server's readiness check on control-plane nodes, the node's Ready state on workers (or, if that proves impractical inside the single throttled restart step, the kubelet health check with the handler comment saying so) — within `microk8s_kubelite_ready_timeout` (ansible/roles/microk8s/defaults/main.yml:256; today's probe selection at ansible/roles/microk8s/handlers/main.yml:72-75).

A node that comes back alive but not ready within the timeout stops the roll and turns the run red, a Friday certs build included; restart and wait remain one throttled task, so the next node never restarts before this one is ready.
The handler comment says what the wait actually checks.

R6 — "docs/runbooks/ has no X.509 counterpart to ssh-host-cert-expiry.md, so a lapsed internal_tls leaf has no documented recovery". Resolved: docs/runbooks/ has that counterpart. It first checks that the host is reachable over SSH and routes a lapsed SSH host cert to `ssh-host-cert-expiry.md`. It names the symptom of a lapsed leaf on each consumer (Proxmox web UI, kubernetes-api.home, the OpenBao listener). It gives `playbooks/renew-internal-tls.yml` as the recovery, stating that a plain renewal run recovers an already-lapsed leaf once the host is reachable.

The runbook spells out that an expired OpenBao listener leaf stops the usual path, because every Jenkins `iac` run fetches its secrets from OpenBao at start, and covers renewing that leaf by hand in that state.
`docs/runbooks/openbao.md`'s "listener cert expired" entry (docs/runbooks/openbao.md:266, today unlinked) points to the new runbook.
